page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.i2ne.xlarge is an x86_64 architecture server powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon 8163 processor running at 2.5 GHz. It features 4 vCPUs derived from 2 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled, alongside a 33 MB L3 cache. The instance is equipped with 32.0 GB of RAM, providing a memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core, and includes 959 GB of local SSD storage. Network performance is defined by a baseline bandwidth of 2 Gbps.

Benchmark results indicate that this instance sits in the lower performance tiers for compute and memory throughput. Single-core and multi-core stress-ng tests place the CPU performance in the bottom 25%, while large-block memory read bandwidth is measured at 20.18 GB/sec, falling into the bottom 10%. Database operations and static web serving throughput also register in the bottom 10% of tested systems, with Redis SET operations achieving 2.97 million operations per second. These metrics highlight a clear tradeoff: while the server offers substantial local storage and memory capacity, its processing power and memory bandwidth are limited.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the ecs.i2ne.xlarge provides a high density of local SSD storage and memory relative to its vCPU count, making it a viable option for workloads that require local data caching or memory-intensive operations without demanding high CPU performance. Appropriate workloads include database hosting, caching layers such as Redis, and general-purpose applications with moderate network and processing requirements.
